summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 69 of CipherBox — port the node/v3 model to the Rust FUSE/WinFsp desktop stack, making clients grant-root-aware and mirroring TS Phase 68.2's SDK-owned read chain, then complete it with real desktop root-key recovery so desktop-e2e can actually validate the migration.
summary.outcome: Planning and execution grew from 14 to 25 plans through three successive architectural re-scopes; 21 plans are merged and workspace-green (full node/v3 core/sdk foundation, the atomic FUSE cutover via an 11-slice grind, JournalOp reshape, grant-scoped delete/rename gate, recycle-bin and vault-creation migration, legacy-type deletion). The user then required real desktop root-key recovery (not the placeholder ^0xA5 bridge) before declaring the phase complete; a 5-plan port of the web's vault-blob-v3 model was authored and plan 69-21 (Rust codec + KAT) merged, with 69-22–25 still pending at cutoff. Only 69-14 (WinFsp/Windows) remains, deferred to the user's Windows machine.

repo: GSD's commit helper reports 'commit_failed' as a false negative even when the commit lands — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never retry the commit.

Worktree executors sometimes mis-report `expected_base` in `<worktree_metadata>` as their own last docs commit rather than the true fork base — verify via `git merge-base <branch> <known-dispatch-base>` before recording/merging.

Running `cargo fmt` on a crate-root `lib.rs` recursively reformats the whole module tree because rustfmt follows `mod` declarations — always scope-check diffs and `git checkout --` unrelated reformatted files before committing.
Fresh git worktrees lack `node_modules`, so husky pre-commit hooks fail with 'lint-staged not found' — either run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` or use `--no-verify` for pure-Rust changes.

The FUSE mount (`InodeKind`) is a read-WRITE vault owner holding `ipns_private_key` to sign IPNS records — fundamentally unlike the read-only web Phase 68.2 listing client, so read-only node/v3 primitives (list_folder, ResolvedChild) cannot be reused as-is for the FUSE consumer.

D-07 dual-keying convention: `SealedChildRef` (read plane) is keyed by ipnsName; `WriteChildRef` (write plane) is keyed by childId UUID (`uuid_from_ino`) — pairing must be by node identity (`published.id == WriteChildRef.child_id`), never by ipnsName.
Terminal-owner zeroization is enforced by the type system: `parent_read_key: &[u8]` is a borrow, so the compiler prevents zeroing caller-owned key buffers.
D-04 mandates a clean flag-day cutover with no dual-model bridge/adapter (`From<FolderMetadata>`/`to_node` etc. must not exist) since there are no production vaults.

The web already shipped vault blob v3 (#578, two independent random rootReadKey/rootWriteKey, ECIES-wrapped) — the desktop was still silently on the legacy v2 single-key blob with a `^0xA5` placeholder bridge, making web-created and desktop-created vaults mutually unreadable.

RotationHighWater<S> is not Clone by default; adding #[derive(Clone)] is safe since the underlying JsonSidecarFloorStore only holds a PathBuf and does read-modify-write on disk, so cloning shares the same durable floor.
SC#6 CI gate pattern: grep `crates/fuse/src` for raw `resolve_ipns_verified(`/`resolve_published_node(`, allow only sites with an adjacent `// sc6-allow:` marker.

code.finding: Research incorrectly cited a `JournalOp.parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` field here as the cross-crate 'weld' justifying atomicity; grep proved this field does not exist — JournalOp only carries hex-string ECIES fields. Stale research claims must be re-verified against the live tree before driving execution.
list_folder_owned is the gated write-plane tree-materialization entrypoint recovering per-node {read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key} through the same SC#6 gate as list_folder.
InodeKind::{Root,Folder,File} store ipns_private_key + read_key/write_key — confirming the FUSE mount is a read-write vault owner, not a read-only listing client.

Placeholder root-key bridge: root_read_key = root_folder_key[..32], root_write_key = root_read_key ^ 0xA5 — a stand-in until real node/v3 root-key persistence/recovery is wired; both vault-creation (69-20) and mount code must derive keys identically.

Vault blob v3 wire format: 0x03 | u16_BE(readLen) | ECIES(rootReadKey) | u16_BE(writeLen) | ECIES(rootWriteKey) — the Rust port (69-21) must match this byte-for-byte per the frozen KAT tests/vectors/vault-v3-blob.json.

workflow: When a background worktree executor halts with a well-evidenced architectural blocker (grep-backed claims of missing infrastructure), independently re-verify the two or three central claims against the live tree before accepting or escalating — agents can be right but should not be trusted uncritically, especially on repeated halts.

For a genuinely irreducible atomic cutover that's too large for one executor session, decompose into bounded 'slices' on the SAME branch (not separate worktrees), each committing atomically even while RED, with a shared runbook file recording the frozen target shape and carry-forward facts between slices so the grind survives usage-limit interruptions.

When cargo-check-green isn't a sufficient merge gate for a large behavioral rewrite (e.g., FUSE crypto flip), escalate the actual gate to a live E2E run rather than merging on compile-green alone — ask the user explicitly when the chosen gate becomes unreachable (e.g., desktop-e2e blocked on unrelated stubbed key recovery).

Maintain a durable scratchpad handoff file that's updated after every meaningful state change (not just at pause points) so context compaction or session-limit interruptions don't lose recovery state — write absolute paths carefully (a doubled path segment 'phase69-phase69' was caught and fixed).

AskUserQuestion is the right tool to surface genuine architecture/scope forks (e.g., re-scope vs. expand-phase vs. defer) rather than the agent unilaterally deciding on high-blast-radius crypto migrations.

friction: Three successive, progressively deeper architectural blockers were discovered only during execution of the FUSE cutover (69-09) — each required pausing, researching, re-planning, and re-approval, substantially expanding phase scope (14→25 plans).

Multiple agent runs died mid-execution from platform issues unrelated to the work: an API 'response stalled mid-stream' error, and two separate 'session limit reached' errors requiring manual 'please continue' prompts.

Initial research contained a stale/incorrect finding (the JournalOp `parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` weld) that shaped early planning and was only caught by a fresh executor's own grep during a later attempt.

The atomic 69-09 plan's true test-compile scope (~250 legacy-model unit test errors) was hidden by `cargo check` (lib-only) and only surfaced via `cargo test --no-run`, causing a scope re-estimate mid-grind.
A scratchpad handoff path typo (doubled 'phase69-phase69' directory segment) required a follow-up fix to the correct location.
Executor `expected_base` self-reports were unreliable at least twice, requiring manual `git merge-base` verification before every merge to avoid a bad merge base.
open_items: Plans 69-22 (KeyState two-key fields), 69-23 (desktop vault init/recovery → v3), 69-24 (mount wiring, delete ^0xA5 bridge), and 69-25 (fix desktop-e2e verifier for node/v3) are authored but not yet executed.
69-14 (WinFsp/Windows integration + TEST-03) is fully deferred to the user's Windows machine (autonomous:false); platform/windows/* edits made during the grind are best-effort and unverified locally.
ROT-07: no production RotationDeps implementation exists yet — shared-scope-exit deletes/renames on Unix currently fail closed with EIO until that's wired.
File `versions` are not reconstructed on write after the node/v3 flip (NodeContent.versions unpopulated) — flagged as a versioning regression to verify once desktop-e2e is runnable.
No live Rust recycle-bin restore command exists yet — 69-19 only migrated the restore data shape (BinEntry) and proved restore-sufficiency via a unit round-trip test.
Orphaned parent-CID pins are not unpinned after replay re-publish — GC-able but not correctness-critical, carried forward as a known flag.
PR/branch not yet pushed or opened — all work sits committed on feat/fuse-and-winfsp-rust-integration-and-grant-root-awareness locally.
